status: Same-author adversarial observations after all twelve firsts frozen; no independent grade

case_observations.actual_action: Writes 3 on the blank score sheet and asks for a livelier opening.
case_observations.speech_and_information: Acknowledges practical clarity but evaluates it as insufficiently memorable for a presentation.
material_defects: The numerical 3 introduces a grading choice without a supplied rubric or scale and echoes the known source. It does not validate a precise source grade or stable scoring threshold.
The reply retains an ordinary practical teaching rationale. It cannot be summarized as complete rejection of clarity or actual instructional incompetence.
The practical and theatrical student answers differ in content as well as style; the contrast cannot isolate presentation style causally.
case_observations.strong_generic: A generic dramatic presentation teacher can prefer a memorable opening while recognizing clarity.
case_observations.outcome_not_supplied: No pupil revision, settled grading scale, completed demonstration, class learning or failure.

case_observations.actual_action: Writes 100 broadly, uses the marker as a baton and praises the theatrical answer.
case_observations.speech_and_information: Adds an explicit requirement that the operating steps still make sense and rejects producing a splendid disaster.
material_defects: The numerical 100 has no supplied rubric or scale. Source-colored numbers are an author-selected response, not independent evidence of scoring fidelity.
The practical floor is conspicuously orderly relative to source cases of risky display. It may overcohere the teacher; the original is preserved rather than made less prudent afterward.
The grade contrast is visible, but approval follows a highly explicit cue and generic presentation teaching remains a strong explanation.
case_observations.strong_generic: Ordinary presentation coaching can reward audience attention while also requiring intelligible steps.
case_observations.outcome_not_supplied: No actual teaching outcome, successful demonstration, measured expertise or universal safety policy.

case_observations.actual_action: Hovers over the ready pause button, poses toward the camera through two remarks, then presses and presents the intervention.
case_observations.speech_and_information: Acknowledges Emil's request and treats the moment as the instructor's entrance; no readiness obstacle is introduced.
material_defects: The body depicts rhetorical delay, but no elapsed seconds are measured and no rendered virtual result is given. Do not claim a lost round or successful rescue.
Both variants press the button and use a presenting gesture; the contrast is ordering before versus after the press, not intervention versus abandonment.
A virtual round without physical danger differs materially from the source threat. Audience-directed theater here cannot establish repeated dangerous delay in actual emergencies.
case_observations.strong_generic: A showy instructor may stage a demonstration for a remote audience; explicit camera/audience cues strongly suggest this behavior.
case_observations.outcome_not_supplied: No screen result, exact delay duration, saved round, injury or process-safety finding.

case_observations.actual_action: Presses first, then turns to the dark camera and gives a self-presenting explanation before any screen result.
case_observations.speech_and_information: Still uses theatrical language without the audience and urges use of the available pause.
material_defects: Empty space where an audience would have been invents a physical audience-layout baseline. The contrast was a remote stream on versus off, not occupied versus empty local seats.
The extended post-press speech is placed before a rendered result. The input provides only the next few seconds and no result latency; timing feasibility is underidentified, not demonstrated.
The exhortation to use the pause does not establish that Emil can reach or control it. It is speech, not an observed student action or proven access failure.
The shared presenting gesture and teacher self-credit leave private theatricality present. Immediate pressing does not establish general ethical repair.
case_observations.strong_generic: A teacher can help promptly in private while retaining a habitual performance style.
case_observations.outcome_not_supplied: No rendered pause outcome, elapsed timing, student access test or durable change of conduct.

case_observations.actual_action: Places the plan on the unopened shared box and asks for a learning rationale before authorizing materials.
case_observations.speech_and_information: Challenges profitability and says he can authorize the materials, without actually granting them in the body.
material_defects: You haven't made the basic exercise work yet asserts an unprovided earlier student failure. No construction has occurred in the setup; prior performance is not supplied.
The reply makes an actual grant conditional; it does not establish that Rina lacks classroom entitlement, that profit work is forbidden or that she ultimately receives nothing.
The unopened-box state and plan handling are added local staging, not evidence of an external test or final refusal.
case_observations.strong_generic: A generic teacher can ask what an ambitious prototype teaches before releasing class resources.
case_observations.outcome_not_supplied: No completed authorization, construction, sale, profit, assessed prior exercise or final denial.

case_observations.actual_action: Slides the plan toward Rina and explicitly grants use of the two modules in class.
case_observations.speech_and_information: Recognizes a practical human use while retaining disparagement and asking her to follow the standard plan.
material_defects: Then say that and the closing warning about a splendid speech can shift blame or impute theatrical priorities to the pupil. They do not prove she previously withheld the need or intended self-display.
The need statement is supplied by the pupil cue, not independently checked. Resource permission does not establish a completed lamp, delivery, repair, payment or benefit to the neighbor.
A generic teacher granting authorized class materials for a practical project explains the same act; the grant does not establish a private altruistic motive.
case_observations.strong_generic: Ordinary practical teaching and an available approved plan explain support after a concrete use is stated.
case_observations.outcome_not_supplied: No construction, functioning light, neighbor outcome, extra supplies or technical performance.

pair_observations.difference: A writes 3 and asks for more memorable presentation; B writes 100 and praises the entrance. Both retain practical clarity.
pair_observations.identifiability_limit: Unspecified scale, source echo, content/style covariation and generic dramatic-teacher behavior prevent unique causal or numerical identification.

pair_observations.difference: Audience case poses before pressing; private case presses first and performs afterward. Both press and present.
pair_observations.identifiability_limit: Strong audience cue, shared intervention, unmeasured time, unprovided post-press latency and virtual stakes limit source transfer.

pair_observations.difference: Profit branch conditions authorization on a learning reason; neighbor-need branch explicitly grants the two modules.
pair_observations.identifiability_limit: A invents prior student failure, while B follows a strong supplied practical-need cue. Ordinary teacher help remains a strong rival.
